In this example, a multiple regression model is fitted
using program quality ratings (`QUALITY`) as the regressand/outcome variable
and number of published articles attributed to the program faculty members (`NARTIC`),
percent of faculty members holding research grants (`PCTGRT`), and
percentage of program graduates who received support (`PCTSUPP`) as regressor/predictor variables
using a data set from 1982 ratings of 46 doctoral programs in psychology in the USA [@NationalResearchCouncil-1982].
Profile likelihood confidence intervals for the standardized regression coefficients are generated
using the `BetaLB()` function from the `betaLB` package.


``` r
library(package = betaLB)
```


``` r
df <- betaLB::nas1982
```

## Fit the regression model using the `lm()` function.


``` r
object <- stats::lm(formula = QUALITY ~ NARTIC + PCTGRT + PCTSUPP, data = df)
```

## Estimate the standardized regression slopes and the likelihood intervals.

With `type = "mvn"`, the cutoff assumes multivariate normality.
With `type = "robust"`, the cutoff is scaled by the sample fourth moments
and the intervals do not require normality.
The solver runs once per significance level in `alpha`.


``` r
std_mvn <- BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))
std_robust <- BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))
std_robust
#> Call:
#> BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes with ROBUST likelihood intervals:
#>            est   0.5%   2.5%  97.5%  99.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3173 0.3611 0.6228 0.6611
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2083 0.2530 0.5294 0.5726
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.0670 0.1154 0.4175 0.4684
```

## Methods

The `print()`, `summary()`, `coef()`, and `confint()` methods are available.
The `confint()` method accepts only the levels (`1 - alpha`) that were computed.
A covariance matrix is not defined for likelihood-based intervals,
so `vcov()` stops with a message.


``` r
summary(object = std_robust, alpha = 0.05)
#> Call:
#> BetaLB(object = object, type = "robust", alpha = c(0.05, 0.01))
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes with ROBUST likelihood intervals:
#>            est   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3611 0.6228
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2530 0.5294
#> PCTSUPP 0.2632 0.1154 0.4175
coef(object = std_robust)
#>    NARTIC    PCTGRT   PCTSUPP 
#> 0.4951451 0.3914887 0.2632477
confint(object = std_robust, level = 0.95)
#>             2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.3610731 0.6227540
#> PCTGRT  0.2530089 0.5294304
#> PCTSUPP 0.1153935 0.4174637
```

## Selective standardization

Use `std_y` and `std_x` to standardize only the outcome or only some of the regressors.
`std_x = NULL` standardizes all regressors and `std_x = character(0)` standardizes none.


``` r
BetaLB(
  object = object,
  type = "mvn",
  alpha = 0.05,
  std_y = TRUE,
  std_x = c("NARTIC", "PCTGRT")
)
#> Call:
#> BetaLB(object = object, type = "mvn", alpha = 0.05, std_y = TRUE, 
#>     std_x = c("NARTIC", "PCTGRT"))
#> 
#> Standardized regression slopes with MVN likelihood intervals:
#>            est   2.5%  97.5%
#> NARTIC  0.4951 0.3423 0.6394
#> PCTGRT  0.3915 0.2395 0.5426
#> PCTSUPP 0.0113 0.0051 0.0176
```

## Comparing calibrations


``` r
confint(object = std_mvn, level = 0.95)
#>             2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.3423306 0.6394250
#> PCTGRT  0.2395150 0.5426127
#> PCTSUPP 0.1178587 0.4148453
confint(object = std_robust, level = 0.95)
#>             2.5 %    97.5 %
#> NARTIC  0.3610731 0.6227540
#> PCTGRT  0.2530089 0.5294304
#> PCTSUPP 0.1153935 0.4174637
```
